name: Question 15
problem: Find a basis of $\,\text{Ker}(T)$ given that $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3y-6z-6x \\ -4y+x+z \\ 2y+8z+8x\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
Finding the kernel of $\,T\,$ is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of $\,T.$

For the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -6 \\ 1 & -4 & 1 \\ 8 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}].$

Setting $x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],$ we then need to solve the equation $Tx=0.$ First, we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -6 \\ 1 & -4 & 1 \\ 8 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{6}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -6 \\ 0 & -\frac{7}{2} & 0 \\ 8 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{4}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -6 \\ 0 & -\frac{7}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{12}{7}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -6 \\ 0 & -\frac{7}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$

From the second equation, we get $y=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we have $x=-z.$ 

Therefore, if $x\in \text{Ker}(T),$ then 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-z \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]z,\,z\in R.
$$

This implies that $B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of $\text{Ker}(T).$

Find a basis of Ker(T) given that T:[xyz]⟶[3y−6z−6x−4y+x+z2y+8z+8x].

EXPLANATION

Finding the kernel of T is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of T.

For the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is T=[−63−61−41828].

Setting x=[xyz], we then need to solve the equation Tx=0. First, we reduce T to row echelon form, as follows:
